correctness.rationale: Each rank-(n−1) isotone map is determined by its unique consecutive double block and its one omitted image value. Idempotence is equivalent to omitting one member of the double block. For the inverse criterion use both cross-transversal conditions: a sandwich identity f g f=f forces g to be injective on im(f) and hence onto im(g) there, and f then maps im(g) bijectively onto im(f). In reverse, with both cross-transversals, the restrictions are increasing bijections between the two ordered images; their composites are identity because increasing bijections of a finite chain to itself are identity. This justifies the criterion without relying on one transversal alone. For x=(j,k) in R, a nonidempotent inverse (u,v) must lie in L since u≥k−1≥j+1≥v, and distinct nonidempotents have no loops. The proposed pairing is feasible, with ψ(u,v)=(v,u+1) its inverse labeling. Every allowed edge has ψ(u,v)≥(j,k) in both coordinates. A perfect matching preserves the sum of each coordinate of R, so every inequality is equality, proving uniqueness. Counting R gives binom(n−1,2), and conjugation by reflection preserves the conditions, hence commutes with the unique matching.
residual_risks: The independent enumeration only covers n=4; the all-n claim rests on the coordinate-sum proof. A single cross-transversal is not sufficient by itself; the joint criterion is valid. Idempotent fixing is essential: swapping the two idempotents sharing a double block gives another inverse involution if it is dropped.

evidence: The rank-(n−1) nonidempotent inverse graph is bipartite. Once idempotents are fixed, uniqueness is exactly uniqueness of a perfect matching on that graph. Higgins's Hall-type results are existence criteria, and the indexed co-rank-one constructions exhibit one such matching.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A literature formulation as unique perfect matching or a forced matching in the same inverse graph would cover the rigidity; a construction of one matching does not. A cyclic-order preserving monoid is not equivalent to the isotone chain monoid under restriction.

value.rationale: An inverse involution known by construction is now forced by a natural fixed-idempotent constraint across an entire canonical Green class, even where vertices have more than one possible inverse partner. That determines the combinatorial freedom in this class, explains equivariance intrinsically, and gives a structural distinction from unconstrained involutions. This value does not rely on the previously known formula being new.
residual_risks: No implication for involutive matching of the entire monoid or rigidity of other ranks is claimed.
